note: An educational catalogue of 22 audiovisual works. A film is a story, never evidence, a scientific study, a legal precedent or a verified account of real events. Nothing here was watched, transcribed or obtained by VIDHI: every entry is registered only, and every description below is a neutral, high-level label for classroom discussion, not a summary of scenes.

exercises.title: The delivery that nobody can prove
exercises.scenario: FICTIONAL SCENARIO written for VIDHI; not from any film. A small shop says it delivered 40 chairs on a Friday. The buyer says only 30 arrived. The shop has a signed slip with no count on it, a photo of stacked chairs with no date, and a driver's message saying 'done'.
questions: Which pieces of evidence say something about the number of chairs, and which only show that a delivery happened?
What one extra document would change how much weight each side's account deserves?

exercises.title: Two accounts of one meeting
exercises.scenario: FICTIONAL SCENARIO written for VIDHI. Two colleagues describe a meeting. One says a deadline was moved to the 20th; the other says it stayed on the 15th. Both kept their own notes, written on different days.
questions: List what the accounts agree on before listing where they differ.
Which differences could be honest memory differences and which would need a document to settle?

exercises.title: Settle now or wait
exercises.scenario: FICTIONAL SCENARIO written for VIDHI. A freelancer is owed a fixed fee. The client offers 80 percent today or nothing certain later. Pursuing the full amount would cost time and some fees.
questions: What does each side gain and lose from waiting?
Which facts are still unknown that would change the choice? Do not give a probability.

exercises.title: The first number
exercises.scenario: FICTIONAL SCENARIO written for VIDHI. A seller opens a negotiation by asking for a very high price, and the buyer's final offer ends up closer to it than the buyer planned.
questions: Which bias might be at work, and what is another explanation that needs no bias?
What could the buyer have prepared before the talk began?

exercises.title: The helpful mistake
exercises.scenario: FICTIONAL SCENARIO written for VIDHI. A bookkeeper notices a customer was charged too little and the error favours the bookkeeper's employer.
questions: Which duties pull in different directions here?
How would two different ethical traditions each describe the right step, without claiming either is proven?

exercises.title: A difficult reminder
exercises.scenario: FICTIONAL SCENARIO written for VIDHI. A supplier needs to remind a long-standing customer about an unpaid invoice without ending the relationship.
questions: What facts and what tone keep the message factual and respectful?
What would make the message read as a threat, and how can that be avoided?

exercises.title: Who decides
exercises.scenario: FICTIONAL SCENARIO written for VIDHI. A committee must choose between two vendors. One member has a past business tie to a vendor but says it does not matter.
questions: What process would make the decision easier to trust?
Which facts should be disclosed and to whom?

exercises.title: Facts first, law second
exercises.scenario: FICTIONAL SCENARIO written for VIDHI. Two people disagree about whether a written agreement was ever signed, and separately about what a clause in it means.
questions: Which part is a dispute about facts and which about interpretation?
What would a lawyer need to look up in a verified source before saying anything about the law? VIDHI does not answer that here.
